content:
Reddit announces two upcoming changes that may upset some long-time users.

The company has already implemented one limitation on Old Reddit, and now it's announcing a second. Additionally, RSS support will also be discontinued…

Old Reddit

Reddit underwent a major user interface redesign in 2018, which was met with strong opposition from users who preferred the original version. In response to this feedback, the platform promised at the time that as long as people were still using it, "Old Reddit" would remain available.

In August, the company began rolling out its first policy change, requiring users of Old Reddit to log in. It is now further announcing that this legacy interface will only be made available to users who have used it within the past six months, with new users being locked out.

Reddit says both changes are aimed at reducing artificial intelligence (AI) scraping of the site's content (though if those companies are willing to pay, it seems that's apparently not a problem at all).

RSS subscription feature to be discontinued

The discontinuation of the RSS subscription feature is based on the same reason.

For some subreddits that rely on RSS for moderation work, this change could cause serious problems. Reddit says it is aware of this situation and suggests moderators use tools like Devvit applications such as Discord Relay.

Users are not too happy

A look at the comments section makes it clear that many long-time users are very unhappy with these latest developments.

What are your thoughts on these latest changes? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
